subject: Ops instrumentation: competitive test plan & next steps
messages:
From: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@dataforge.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: Quick recap + ask from today's call

Hi Neha and team,

Thanks for the demo today — the latency numbers and dedicated routing options look promising. To help our infra and security teams finish the evaluation, we need a short checklist and some concrete tests comparing Redwood against the hyperscaler endpoints we're also validating (AWS Bedrock + Google Vertex AI). Specifically:

- Observability: what telemetry (metrics/traces/logs) do you expose by default?
- Tracing integration: do you emit OpenTelemetry spans and which fields are included (trace_id, span_id, model, shard)?
- Usage analytics: sample request/response logs, token breakdowns, per-route cost breakdowns (anonymized).
- Error surface: how do you surface timeouts, OOMs, and model fallback events?

Can you share a short test plan (3–5 tests) we can run in our eval window next week and any sample artifacts (schema, example payloads)? Procurement may also request an instrumented PII/non-PII data handling note.

Appreciate an itemized follow-up we can circulate internally.

Thanks,
Alex
Alex Nguyen
Director of AI Platforms | DataForge

--
Attachment: none (will accept your matrix/statements)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@dataforge.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>, Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 9 Nov 2026 17:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask from today's call

Alex — thanks for the clear list. Quick internal note and proposed plan below; attaching a compact telemetry matrix and a candidate test-case doc.

Summary (short):
- Default telemetry: latency histograms (p50/p95/p99), per-request token counts, model id, instance id, endpoint / route, error codes, and sampling of response hashes for reruns.
- Tracing: full OpenTelemetry-compatible spans. We propagate trace_id/span_id and include attributes: model.version, shard_id, prompt_length, kv_cache_hit (boolean). Spans are emitted for request queueing, model dispatch, token generation, and response finalization.
- Usage analytics: tokenized cost breakdown, per-token compute time, aggregated per-route cost. Exports are available as CSVs and via the Console API.
- Error surface: explicit events for Timeout, OutOfMemory, KernelFallback; each includes instance_id, queued_time, and stack-sampled reason when available.

Proposed evaluation tests (3 recommended, run in sequence):
1) Observability baseline: send 1k varied-length requests (5–512 tokens), validate metrics emitted (latency percentiles, per-model counts), confirm trace_id continuity across retries.
2) Tracing fidelity: issue 200 concurrent requests with parent trace injection; verify spans show model.version and kv_cache_hit attribute; confirm trace captures fallback events when we intentionally create OOM pressure.
3) Cost/analytics reconciliation: run a 2-hour burst workload and reconcile per-token compute time and cost from Redwood Console exports vs your ingestion.

Operational notes:
- We recommend allowing prefix caching to be disabled for parity with hyperscaler baselines; we can toggle this at route level.
- We'll provide a temporary instrumented webhook for streaming event exports so your telemetry pipeline can ingest directly.

Next steps / owners:
- Ben: add low-level test scripts (curl + otel headers) and a small harness + expected schema (ETA: Tue EOD).
- Diego: prepare short runbook on how to force/fake OOM and fallback behavior in Dedicated/Hosted (ETA: Tue noon).
- Marissa: coordinate POC window and SSO/ACL notes with procurement (ETA: Wed).

Attached: telemetry-matrix-v1.xlsx, redwood-vs-hyperscaler-test-cases.md

I'll follow up with a short calendar invite for a 30-min alignment on test orchestration.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Head of Solutions, Redwood Inference
neha.kapoor@redwood.ai

--
Attachments: telemetry-matrix-v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 12KB), redwood-vs-hyperscaler-test-cases.md (markdown, 4KB)

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, Alex Nguyen <alex.nguyen@dataforge.com>
Cc: Diego Fernandez <diego.fernandez@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Nov 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick recap + ask from today's call

Adding the test-harness notes here so Alex has something to run quickly. I'll drop the repo link in the Drive folder. Short checklist for each test:

Observability baseline (script: run_obs_baseline.sh)
- Payloads: 1000 requests (randomized lengths)
- Headers: x-otel-traceparent header included for each request
- Validate: presence of p50/p95/p99 in metrics endpoint, per-route token counts match request log

Tracing fidelity (script: run_trace_check.sh)
- Use Otel SDK to inject parent span (trace_id)
- Trigger fallback by sending oversized context in a small Dedicated flavor (we'll provide the endpoint)
- Validate attributes: model.version, shard_id, kv_cache_hit, fallback.reason present on fallback span

Cost reconciliation (script: run_cost_recon.sh)
- Start 2h burst at rated concurrency; collect console export after run
- Compare to local token accounting (script outputs CSV)

Notes:
- We'll provide pre-built curl examples; if you want we can also run the harness from our side and share the raw telemetry exports to speed things up.
- Security note: telemetry samples will be sanitized to remove prompt text unless you request full payloads under an NDA.

I'll have the scripts + example output uploaded to the Drive by Tue EOD. Planning a 30-min sync tomorrow 11:00am PT to walk through execution (invite to follow).

-Ben
Ben Carter
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
